analysis:
Ahead of the 2008 Delhi Assembly elections, the Sheila Dikshit government issued provisional regularisation certificates to 1,639 unauthorised colonies and promised to regularise them if the Congress returned to power. The Economic Times report notes that no colony had been regularised before 2012.

On 28 August 2012 Chief Minister Dikshit announced the regularisation of 917 of those colonies, and said the government was "fulfilling the promise it made in 2008". A section of colonies (on Archaeological Survey of India or forest land) was left out, and another report records that some colonies received provisional certificates despite incomplete applications.

In February 2014 the Delhi government sought action against Dikshit following a Lokayukta order on the regularisation of unauthorised colonies. The full set of colonies covered by the 2008 promise had not been regularised by the end of the term, and the process continued under later governments.
notes: The 2008 promise predates the 28 August 2012 announcement; the claim date is set to November 2008 (before the assembly polls) and is approximate. The exact wording of the 2008 promise was not located in a primary transcript, so quote_is_verbatim is false. Verdict 'unachieved' reflects partial delivery (917 of 1,639 by 2012) rather than total failure.
